findings.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:78 — POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup response now includes plaintext `backupCodes` array in the JSON body with no API version bump or schema doc update; any external/API-docs consumer that logs or persists the full response verbatim (e.g. support tooling, mobile client caching responses) would now capture sensitive backup codes it never expected to receive

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:65 — NextAuth credentials provider gains a new `backupCode` credential field alongside existing `email`/`password`/`totpCode`; since it's optional and only branches on `credentials.backupCode` truthiness, existing callers of the credentials sign-in (CLI login, other API clients) that don't send it are unaffected

packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:1 — Migration adds nullable `backupCodes` column with no backfill, so all existing `twoFactorEnabled: true` users retain `backupCodes: NULL` and cannot use backup-code recovery until they manually re-run 2FA setup (setup.ts only writes backupCodes on next enable)

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:63 — backupCodes` state is declared as `useState([])` with no `string[]` type annotation, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and later `.map(formatBackupCode)` calls are untyped/`any`, silently defeating type-checking on this security-sensitive data

apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:51 — throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` on missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not wrapped in try/catch, so unlike every other branch in this handler (which returns res.status(...).json(...)), it produces an unhandled exception that Next.js turns into a generic framework 500 instead of the handler's normal JSON error shape.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:150 — Single-use enforcement of backup codes (setting the consumed code to null and re-encrypting) is never tested, so a regression allowing code reuse would go undetected

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:110 — Backup code format (`XXXXX-XXXXX`) and actual content are never asserted; both the downloaded file content and clipboard content are left as TODOs, so the codes shown to the user could be malformed/wrong and tests would still pass

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:78 — POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup response now includes plaintext `backupCodes` array in the JSON body with no API version bump or schema doc update; any external/API-docs consumer that logs or persists the full response verbatim (e.g. support tooling, mobile client caching responses) would now capture sensitive backup codes it never expected to receive

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` to return `backupCodes` in plaintext in the JSON response (`return res.json({ secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes });`) after generating them server-side. That’s a potentially sensitive-contract change (similar to already returning `secret`), but the claims about “no API version bump” and “schema doc update” and downstream consumers logging/persisting the response are not verifiable from this diff alone, making it more of an integration/contract concern than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:1 — disable endpoint now accepts an additional optional `backupCode` field in the request body; old clients omitting it fall through to the pre-existing TOTP branch (`else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)`), so this is backward compatible

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the new optional `backupCode` handling (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode) ... else if (user.twoFactorEnabled) ...`) which would indeed fall back to the existing TOTP branch when `backupCode` is omitted. However, this is not a review issue/defect or an actionable concern—it's merely a compatibility observation—so it doesn't fit "bug" or "important_non_bug".

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode.ts:11 — Two new error codes `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` are added to the shared ErrorCode enum returned by both the REST disable endpoint and the NextAuth credentials `authorize()` callback; any external client that maps ErrorCode values to UI copy (e.g. a future mobile client) must be updated to handle these new string values or will show a generic/unknown-error fallback for backup-code failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new shared `ErrorCode` enum values (`IncorrectBackupCode`, `MissingBackupCodes`) in `packages/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode.ts` and actively returns/throws them from both the REST disable endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`) and the NextAuth credentials `authorize()` flow (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`). This is an API/contract expansion: any other consumer that switches/maps on `ErrorCode` strings and lacks handling for these new values would fall back to a generic error. That’s a compatibility consideration rather than a defect in this PR itself, and the PR already updates the web UI to handle these errors in `login.tsx` and `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:65 — NextAuth credentials provider gains a new `backupCode` credential field alongside existing `email`/`password`/`totpCode`; since it's optional and only branches on `credentials.backupCode` truthiness, existing callers of the credentials sign-in (CLI login, other API clients) that don't send it are unaffected

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an optional `backupCode` credential and the logic only enters the backup-code path when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is truthy; otherwise it falls back to the existing TOTP path (`else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)`). So the statement that callers not sending `backupCode` are unaffected is accurate, but it does not describe a defect or actionable review issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:205 — New `backupCodes String?` column added to User model; not found to be selected by any public user-facing serializer/select-star query in this repo (no public API package references two-factor fields), so no evidence of unintended exposure, but this should be explicitly verified against any `select: { ...allFields }` patterns outside this diff before considering it safe long-term

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the new `backupCodes` field is “not found to be selected by any user-facing serializer/select query,” but the diff explicitly selects it in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (`select: { ... backupCodes: true }`) and returns `backupCodes` to the client from the setup endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` returns `{ ..., backupCodes }`). The rest of the finding is an unverified “check outside this diff” suggestion, which cannot be validated from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:1 — Migration adds nullable `backupCodes` column with no backfill, so all existing `twoFactorEnabled: true` users retain `backupCodes: NULL` and cannot use backup-code recovery until they manually re-run 2FA setup (setup.ts only writes backupCodes on next enable)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `users.backupCodes` column with no backfill (migration.sql) and only populates it during 2FA setup (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` generates and encrypts backup codes). Login/disable flows explicitly error when `backupCodes` is missing (`MissingBackupCodes` in `next-auth-options.ts` and `totp/disable.ts`). So existing `twoFactorEnabled` users will indeed have `backupCodes = NULL` and cannot use the new backup-code path unless they re-run 2FA setup (or otherwise regenerate codes). This is a backwards-compatibility/product completeness gap rather than a strict defect, since backup-code recovery didn’t exist previously and the code handles the null case with a specific error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:1 — No down/rollback migration file accompanies this migration, so reverting the deploy requires a manually authored DROP COLUMN statement

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a standard Prisma migration at `packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql` with an `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` statement. Prisma migrations in this repo structure are one-way SQL files within a timestamped folder; the diff does not show (nor does Prisma typically require) a separate down/rollback migration file alongside it. The finding asserts a missing companion rollback file, which is not something evidenced or required by what’s shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:63 — backupCodes` state is declared as `useState([])` with no `string[]` type annotation, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and later `.map(formatBackupCode)` calls are untyped/`any`, silently defeating type-checking on this security-sensitive data

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx the state is declared as `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` (no generic like `useState<string[]>([])`). Since `body` comes from `await response.json()` (implicitly `any`), `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` accepts whatever shape without compile-time validation, and later `backupCodes.map((code) => formatBackupCode(code))` is not type-protected against non-string elements. This is a type-safety gap rather than a proven runtime defect given the API currently returns strings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:51 — throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` on missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not wrapped in try/catch, so unlike every other branch in this handler (which returns res.status(...).json(...)), it produces an unhandled exception that Next.js turns into a generic framework 500 instead of the handler's normal JSON error shape.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the newly added backup-code path does `if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) { ...; throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError); }` (around the added block starting near line 51). In the shown handler code, other error cases return `res.status(...).json({ error: ... })` (e.g., incorrect password / missing code / incorrect TOTP), and there is no evidence in the diff of an outer try/catch that would convert this throw into the same JSON error shape. As written, this throw would bubble out and result in a generic Next.js 500 response rather than the handler’s normal `{ error: ErrorCode... }` payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:150 — Single-use enforcement of backup codes (setting the consumed code to null and re-encrypting) is never tested, so a regression allowing code reuse would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds single-use consumption logic for backup codes in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (within `authorize`): it finds the matching code, then sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and persists the updated encrypted list via `prisma.user.update(...)`. The only added e2e coverage in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` exercises displaying/downloading/copying/closing backup codes, and even includes a `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup` comment—there is no test that verifies a backup code cannot be reused after being consumed. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly introduced security-relevant logic, not a current functional defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:110 — Backup code format (`XXXXX-XXXXX`) and actual content are never asserted; both the downloaded file content and clipboard content are left as TODOs, so the codes shown to the user could be malformed/wrong and tests would still pass

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` the newly added backup-code checks only assert the download filename and that a success toast appears after clicking copy; the comments explicitly leave `// TODO: check file content` and `// TODO: check clipboard content` (around the added section after enabling 2FA). There is also no assertion that the UI shows the expected `XXXXX-XXXXX` formatting produced by `formatBackupCode` in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`. So malformed/incorrect backup code output could slip through while the test still passes.
